chapterFiles.title: Matthew 1 — Genealogy of Jesus + the virgin-birth narrative
Matthew 2 — The magi and the star, the flight into Egypt, the return to Nazareth
Matthew 3 — John the Baptist, and the baptism of Jesus: the heavens opened
Matthew 4 — The temptation in the wilderness, the move to Capernaum, the first disciples
Matthew 5 — Sermon on the Mount Pt I: Beatitudes, salt and light, 'not to abolish but to fulfill,' the antitheses
Matthew 6 — Sermon on the Mount Pt II: alms, the Lord's Prayer, fasting, treasure in heaven, anxiety
Matthew 7 — Sermon on the Mount Pt III: judgment, ask-seek-knock, the golden rule, the narrow gate, the two builders
Matthew 8 — Healings (the leper, the centurion's servant), the stilling of the sea, the Gadarene demoniacs
Matthew 9 — The paralytic forgiven and raised, the call of Matthew, the ruler's daughter, the woman healed, the blind and the mute
Matthew 10 — The sending of the twelve: authority, instructions, persecution, and what to fear
Matthew 13 — The kingdom parables: Sower (Raëlian-canon panspermia site), Tares, Mustard Seed, Leaven, Hidden Treasure, Pearl, Net
Matthew 14 — The death of John the Baptist, the feeding of the five thousand, walking on the sea
Matthew 15 — What defiles a person, the Canaanite woman, healings on the mountain, the feeding of the four thousand
Matthew 17 — The Transfiguration + the demoniac boy + the temple-tax
Matthew 19 — Marriage and divorce, the children, the rich young man, the first and the last
Matthew 23 — Against the scribes and Pharisees: one teacher, one Father, the woes, and the lament over Jerusalem
Matthew 25 — Ten Virgins + Talents + Sheep and Goats (the final judgment)
Matthew 26 — The anointing at Bethany, the last supper, Gethsemane, the arrest ('more than twelve legions of angels'), the trial before Caiaphas, Peter's denial
Matthew 27 — Judas's end, the trial before Pilate and Barabbas, the crucifixion, the darkness and the earthquake, the burial and the guard
Matthew 28 — The Resurrection + the Great Commission

subtitles.en: Every Matthew chapter the Raëlian canon cites (1–10, 13–15, 17, 19, 23, 25–28): the birth and the magi, the baptism and the temptation, the Sermon on the Mount, the healings and the sending of the twelve, the parables, the Transfiguration, the passion and the Resurrection

descriptions.en:
An English translation of the eight Matthew chapters most heavily engaged by the Raëlian canon — produced from the earliest substantial Koine Greek manuscript witnesses (4th c. CE uncials Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, cross-collated against the 2nd-3rd c. CE papyri P45, P64+P67, P77, P103, P104). **The project's first Christian-tradition text** and **first Koine Greek source text**.

The 8 canon-cited chapters: **Mt 1** (genealogy of Jesus + the virgin-birth narrative); **Mt 5** (Sermon on the Mount Pt I: Beatitudes, salt and light, 'not to abolish but to fulfill,' the antitheses); **Mt 6** (Sermon on the Mount Pt II: alms, the Lord's Prayer, fasting, treasure in heaven, anxiety); **Mt 7** (Sermon on the Mount Pt III: judgment, ask-seek-knock, the golden rule, the narrow gate, the two builders); **Mt 13** (the kingdom parables — the Parable of the Sower is **the canon's explicit panspermia-citation site** per Raël's reading as 'life being seeded on multiple worlds'); **Mt 17** (the Transfiguration + the demoniac boy + the temple-tax); **Mt 25** (Ten Virgins + Talents + Sheep and Goats — the final-judgment chapter); **Mt 28** (the Resurrection + the Great Commission).

The **early-manuscript approach** parallels the Qur'an translation's Tübingen Ma VI 165 + Codex Parisino-petropolitanus method: source the text from the earliest substantially-complete codices (Vaticanus 4th c., Sinaiticus 4th c.), cross-collate against the earlier papyri where they preserve target verses (P104 ~150 CE is among the earliest witnesses to Matthew — earlier than both uncials by ~150-200 years), and document NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical-apparatus variants per verse.

**Fourth canon-source-tension closure** after Shi'ur Qomah (*parasangs*), Qur'an (*inshiqāq al-qamar* + *ḥūr ʿīn*), and Exodus (pillar/parting/manna/theophany). The acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework is applied at the Mt 13 Parable-of-the-Sower panspermia-site + Mt 17 Transfiguration + Mt 28 Resurrection + Great Commission canon-engagement sites — same pattern.

The WoH-Translation produces the philologically-disciplined version with explicit operational disavowals against (a) the Raëlian-canon Mt 13 panspermia pre-resolution; (b) Christian-supersessionist readings (Mt 5:17 'not to abolish but to fulfill' must NOT be theologized into 'Old-Testament-superseded'); (c) the Isa 7:14 LXX-*parthenos* vs Hebrew *ʿalmâ* virgin-birth philological dispute preserved-not-adjudicated; (d) Sitchin/Anunnaki-engineered-spiritual-technology pre-resolution; (e) the orientalist/colonialist Great-Commission misreadings.
descriptions.verificationNote: This translation is produced from a best-effort reconstruction based on the earliest substantial Koine Greek manuscript witnesses. The text is well-attested across Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + the early papyri; variants where they exist are documented per verse. Verification against the original manuscript codicology (Vatican Library Gr. 1209; British Library Add. 43725 + the Sinai/Leipzig/St. Petersburg Sinaiticus folios; Chester Beatty Library P45; Magdalen College P64; Oxford P.Oxy P77/P103/P104) is pending. The NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT/THGNT critical apparatuses are referenced for variants.
descriptions.lensRiskNote: Matthew translation carries a distinctive lens-risk landscape: (a) the Raëlian-canon Mt 13 Parable-of-the-Sower panspermia-citation (Raël: 'life being seeded on multiple worlds') — major lens-risk site, acknowledgment-without-endorsement applied; (b) Christian-supersessionist readings (Mt 5:17 + the antitheses; the Sheep-and-Goats Final Judgment; Mt 28 Great Commission) — explicitly disavowed; (c) Sitchin/Anunnaki-engineered-spiritual-technology — explicitly disavowed; (d) the Isa 7:14 LXX-*parthenos* (virgin) vs Hebrew *ʿalmâ* (young woman) virgin-birth philological dispute preserved-not-adjudicated; (e) the Transfiguration NT-theological vs literal-glory crux preserved; (f) orientalist/colonialist Great-Commission misreadings. The Editor and Reviewer pipeline produces named-scholarship attributions at every claim site (Davies-Allison ICC, Luz Hermeneia, France NICNT, Hagner WBC, Nolland NIGTC, Brown Anchor, Levine-Brettler JANT).
